title: flashpaged-prefetch-sensitivity-journal
content:
High-level goal:
Investigate intermittent tail-latency spikes observed in production for long-sequence workloads when using FlashAttention + paged attention fallback and a new fused-ops kernel chain. Determine sensitivity surface for prefetch/page size/kv-allocation heuristics and propose concrete mitigation steps (config and code changes).

Summary / TL;DR:
- Reproduced p95/p99 spikes on local 4xA100 testbed with llama-2-7b-like model and synthetic seq-length mix matching traffic (mostly 64/128, occasional 512/1024).
- Root cause appears to be interaction between paged attention page faults (software-managed page pop/prefetch), fused-op kernel launch ordering, and slab fragmentation in the KV allocator.
- FlashAttention is fastest for medium sequences (<=256) but when the runtime switches to paged attention for >512, the prefetch policy and small-page thrashing cause 2-4x p99 regressions for single-request bursts.
- Fused ops reduce overall token-wall-time but increase occupancy variance; combined with page prefetching they cause kernel queue stalls that amplify stragglers under continuous-batching.

Test rig and reproducibility notes:
- Hardware: 4xA100 40GB (DGX-ish), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.1, NCCL 2.18. Kernel build: custom runtime branch flashpaged-experiments (see PR 4123).
- Model: distilled checkpoint architecture matching 7B decoder-only (attention dims 4096, kv cache per-layer ~512KB for seq=1024).
- Workload generator: sequence-mixer script (attached in linked_artifacts) to replay production mix: 70% seq<=128, 20% seq=512, 10% seq>=1024. Burst patterns: poisson arrivals lambda=0.8rps per GPU.
- Profiling: nv-nsight (system-level traces), CUPTI kernel timelines, nvprof for kernel-level breakdowns, and custom nvtx markers instrumented around allocator/prefetch calls. Also captured kernel selection logs with verbose=3.

Experiment matrix (representative runs):
- Variables: batch_size {1,4,8}, seq_cutoff_for_paged {384,512,768}, prefetch_pages {0,1,2,4}, kv_slab_size {2MB,4MB,8MB}, fused_ops_enabled {on,off}
- Each point: 10k requests or 30 minutes wall time, record p50/p95/p99, CPU-side scheduling delays, kernel queue depth, SM occupancy variance, page-unmap/refault counts.

Notable results (select comparisons):
1) Baseline (fused_ops=on, seq_cutoff=512, prefetch=1, slab=4MB):
   - batch=1: p50 38ms, p95 220ms, p99 540ms (spike clusters around burst edges)
   - batch=4: p50 44ms, p95 270ms, p99 620ms
2) Disable fused ops (fused_ops=off, keep others):
   - batch=1: p50 42ms, p95 180ms, p99 320ms (p99 improved substantially)
   - Observation: more kernels overall but less historic long-tail; suggests fused ops amplified stall amplification when page faults/prefetch collide.
3) Increase prefetch pages to 4 (fused_ops=on):
   - batch=1: p50 40ms, p95 200ms, p99 390ms (improved vs prefetch=1)
   - but memory pressure increased; observed occasional OOM-like GC of slab allocator under sustained seq=1024 mix.
4) Raise seq_cutoff_for_paged to 768 (favor FlashAttention up to 768):
   - batch=1: p99 drops to ~280ms, p95 ~160ms.
   - But FlashAttention kernel uses more peak memory with long-prefix coalescing; careful with multi-tenant capacity planning.
5) Small slab size (2MB) causes frequent slab recycling, higher allocator lock contention and higher p99. Larger slab (8MB) smooths p99 but increases peak memory and fragmentation later.

Hypotheses and evidence:
- Hyp 1: Kernel launch ordering between fused-ops chain and prefetch IO causes GPUs to enter serialization points (kernels waiting on page fill completion), producing stragglers. Evidence: NSight timeline shows fused-op kernels submit a tight sequence of launches; when page-prefetch latency increases (~2–5ms/page) later kernels pile up behind a completion event.
- Hyp 2: KV allocator slab recycling frequency correlates with p99 spikes. Evidence: nvtx markers for slab alloc/free show bursts aligned with p99 spikes; tracer shows lock hold times increased in those periods.
- Hyp 3: Continuous batching interacts poorly with variable per-request prefetch needs; a single slow paged-request amplifies latency of coalesced batch. Evidence: experiments with batch 4 show higher p99 multiplicative factor compared to batch 1, and metrics indicate batch-coalescer waits for the slowest request to finish.

Micro-observations / weirdness (informal notes):
- Some p99 spikes persist even with prefetch=4; examining kernel selection logs revealed sporadic fallback to a debug-paged kernel (older code path) triggered by a heuristic mis-evaluating model-layer size. There might be a race where kernel-selector cache isn't invalidated after model-quantization change. Filed PR#4123 to guard selector invariants.
- On a run with sequence plateauing for ~5 minutes, the runtime started grouping requests into a "long-seq favored" scheduling domain. Not sure if scheduler learned state or a side-effect of memory allocator warm-up.
- Fused-op binary compiled with -O3 sometimes yields more divergent SM occupancy than -O2; recompilation toggles changed tail behaviour slightly. Need deterministic CI builds for kernel experiments.

Actionable mitigations (short-term):
1) Increase seq_cutoff_for_paged to 768 or higher for current traffic profile to favor FlashAttention for mixed workloads (config change). Immediate effect: reduces p99 by ~30–50% in tests.
2) Expose prefetch_pages as runtime knob per-customer; default to 2 rather than 1. Trade-off between p99 and memory.
3) Add jitter to fused-op kernel submission to avoid tight chains blocking prefetch completion (experimental flag fused-op-stagger).
4) Increase default slab size to 8MB for now to reduce allocator churn; monitor memory budgets.
5) Hotfix PR to kernel selector cache invalidation (see linked PR).

Actionable mitigations (medium-term / code):
- Rework prefetch policy: make it asynchronous with a dedicated IO worker queue that can prioritize prefetches for oldest requests first. Avoid synchronous prefetch in the critical path of kernel submission.
- Make fused-op kernel chain resilient: break chain into micro-batches so that a stall from a single page fault doesn't block unrelated layers/kernels. Consider a cooperative yield model where kernels that detect pending page-prefetch can yield.
- Improve allocator: adopt span-based allocator to reduce lock contention and make slab recycling less frequent; add metrics and high-resolution tracing hooks for allocator internals.

Open questions / follow-up experiments:
- How does multi-tenant resource isolation (cgroups / memlimit) interact with prefetch memory pressure? We need runs with simulated tenants enabled.
- Can we implement a cheap kernel-level speculative prefetch that overlaps with compute for neighboring layers without needing full paged-engine involvement?
- Is there a simple scheduling heuristic to prevent coalescing a large long-seq request into a small-seq batch (prefer batching like-sized requests)?
- Quantify cost delta: raising seq_cutoff reduces p99 but increases token-cost due to less-efficient FlashAttention for very long prefix combos—need billing model impact analysis.

Notes to self / Triage for next week:
- Reproduce the selector-cache-invalidation failure in a minimized unit test; attach to PR 4123. (Claire)
- Run multi-tenant sim with mem-isolation (Diego).
- Prototype fused-op-stagger (Asha) and measure p99 improvement at batch=4 with prefetch=1.
- Add allocator nvtx markers and a histogram for lock hold times (Samir).

Relevant logs / commands used for profiling (copyable):
- nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=none --duration=1800 ./bin/replay_workload --config workload.yaml
- python -m perf_extract kernel_timeline run1.qdrep --nvtx-filter "allocator|prefetch|kernel_selector"
- ./scripts/sequence-mixer --seed 42 --rps 0.8 --mix-file mixes/nov-dec.json > load.log
- export RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selector:3,allocator:2,prefetch:2

Historic context / related docs:
- This intersects with prior notes on "kv-prefetch-tuning-and-flashattention-tradeoffs" (search drive) but is intentionally focusing on the operator-interaction surface (fused-op + paged prefetch + allocator) rather than microkernel latency.

Conclusions (working):
- Short-term config changes (raise seq cutoff, bump prefetch default, increase slab) give quick wins for p99 without code changes.
- Medium-term work on prefetch architecture and allocator will be necessary to handle sustained long-seq mixes at scale and to make fused ops robust.
- Avoid premature disabling of fused ops in production; instead roll experimental flags with telemetry to detect amplification cases.

Appendix: sample p99 trace excerpt (human-readable event timeline):
- t=0.00ms kernel_launch fused-layer-3 (flash)
- t=0.22ms nvtx allocator:ensure_kv_page layer3 (allocated slab page id=31)
- t=1.4ms prefetch->kick io-thread page_request id=31 (async)
- t=1.9ms fused-chain submit layers 4..6
- t=3.5ms page_fill complete (2.1ms latency)
- t=3.51ms fused-chain layer 4 enters compute
- t=7.9ms fused-chain layer 6 waits on barrier -> queue stall (other streams blocked waiting for slot)

If anything in this doc looks useful to formalize into the playbook, we should promote the short-term mitigations to the runbook and add dashboards for allocator churn and prefetch latency.

End of notes.
